title: ChatGPT and learning from human feedback (RLHF)
idea: A language model learns to be a helpful assistant from people who rank its answers: a second model learns their preferences, and the first is trained to please it. ChatGPT, released in November 2022, put this kind of assistant in front of millions of people.

cameFrom.note: The starting point is a large pre-trained GPT model, which can write fluently but does not reliably do what it is asked.

cameFrom.label: Learning from human preferences (Christiano and colleagues, 2017)
cameFrom.note: Researchers at OpenAI and DeepMind had trained agents from people's choices between pairs of behaviours. OpenAI later used the method to train summaries (2020).

cameFrom.label: Reinforcement learning (PPO, 2017)
cameFrom.note: A standard method for improving a system by trial and reward, used here with the learned preferences as the reward.

people.note: Researcher at OpenAI and first author of the InstructGPT paper, which described the method behind ChatGPT.

papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022); arXiv:2203.02155
papers.summary: It fine-tuned GPT-3 with written demonstrations and with people's rankings of its answers, producing models called InstructGPT. People preferred the answers of a 1.3 billion parameter InstructGPT model to those of the original 175 billion parameter GPT-3. OpenAI trained ChatGPT later that year with the same methods, adapted for conversation.

steps.heading: Start from a big model
steps.body: A pre-trained GPT model already knows a lot about language, but it continues text rather than answering the request.

steps.heading: Show it good answers
steps.body: People write example answers to a range of prompts, and the model is fine-tuned to imitate them.

steps.heading: Ask people to rank
steps.body: The model writes several answers to the same prompt and people rank them from best to worst. Ranking is easier and more consistent than writing.

steps.heading: Learn the preferences
steps.body: A second network, the reward model, is trained to predict which answer people would prefer, giving any answer a score.

steps.heading: Optimise against the scores
steps.body: The language model is trained with reinforcement learning (PPO) to write answers the reward model scores highly. A penalty keeps it from drifting too far from its starting point, which would let it exploit quirks of the reward model.

steps.heading: Limits
steps.body: The model learns what raters prefer, which is not the same as what is true. It can still state falsehoods confidently, and it inherits the raters' blind spots.
